name: false_sharing_counters
task: This project computes summary statistics (sum, count above a threshold, count of even values) over a large array of integers, split across multiple translation units: include/data_gen.h + src/data_gen.cpp (a deterministic random-array generator), include/stats.h + src/stats.cpp (serial and OpenMP-parallel statistics), include/report.h + src/report.cpp (a text formatter), and src/main.cpp (the profiling entry point). compute_stats_parallel() in src/stats.cpp gives every thread a slot in a tightly packed std::vector<Stats> (24 bytes per slot) and updates partial[t] on every loop iteration. Slots of neighbouring threads share 64-byte cache lines, so every write invalidates the line in the other cores' caches (false sharing). The result is numerically correct but the parallel version is many times slower than a version without false sharing. The test harness compares compute_stats_parallel() with a reference implementation that performs the same per-iteration updates on cache-line-padded per-thread slots and requires it to be at most 2.5x slower (best of 7 runs, 12M elements); this timing check is skipped on machines with fewer than 4 hardware threads. Fix compute_stats_parallel() so it keeps returning exactly the same Stats as compute_stats_serial() but no longer suffers from false sharing (for example accumulate in local variables and write the slot once after the loop, use an OpenMP reduction, or pad/align each slot to a cache line), keeping the loop parallelized with OpenMP. Do not change any function signature or the Stats layout declared in include/stats.h, include/report.h or include/data_gen.h.
notes: build_command compiles the profiling entry point at build/app (src/main.cpp -> data_gen.cpp, stats.cpp, report.cpp). This binary must be built and then executed via run_command to drive DiscoPoP's instrumentation and produce its dynamic profiling output, including dynamic_dependencies, over the parallel accumulation loop in compute_stats_parallel(). test_command builds and runs a separate correctness harness at build/run_tests (from tests/test_main.cpp); it is independent of the profiling binary and should not be used as the DiscoPoP execution target. Both binaries link the same data_gen.cpp, stats.cpp, report.cpp object files, so no separate CMake/Meson/etc. configuration is required — plain 'make' is sufficient to build, run, and test.
